candidates.file: Flag of the Governor-General of Pakistan (1947-1953).svg
candidates.text: ! scope="row" | |1947–1953 |The flag from 1947 to 1956, the governor-general of Pakistan used a dark blue flag bearing the royal crest (a lion standing on the Crown), beneath which was the word 'PAKISTAN' in gold majuscules. The same design is still used by many other governors-general. This last flag was the personal flag of the governor-general only. This flag was used from 1947 until 1952. |}

! scope="row" | |2005–present |Flag of Sindh |A traditional green flag, with the provincial emblem in the centre.

! scope="row" | |1970–present |Flag of Punjab |A traditional green flag, with the provincial emblem in the centre. The emblem reflects Punjab's natural resources: its wheat, and the five rivers which give the province its name in Persian (from Punj = Five, Aab = Waters).

! scope="row" | |2011–present |Flag of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa |A traditional green flag, with the provincial emblem on the flag shows the Jamrud fort which guards the Khyber Pass, and mountains in the back.

! scope="row" | |2005–present |Flag of Balochistan |A traditional green flag, with the provincial emblem in the centre. The emblem shows stylised mountains of this barren province and the principal mode of transport: the Dromedary camel, also the provincial animal of Balochistan.

! scope="row" | |2011–present |Flag of Gilgit-Baltistan |A traditional green flag, with the provincial emblem on the flag showing the Baltit Fort and the Skardu Fort which guards the Himalayas (including K2), the designated national peak in the back.

! scope="row" | |1975–present |Flag of Azad Kashmir |The flag displays the Pakistani national colours, white and dark green, with a crescent and star to represent the Muslim majority, and a saffron square to represent the Buddhist, Hindu, Sikh, and other minorities of the disputed region, the colours are clearly influenced by the Mughal Empire. The four white stripes symbolise the main rivers of the Kashmir region; Indus, Jhelum, Chenab and Ravi. It also represents the five geographic divisions of the disputed territory, Baltistan, Gilgit, Jammu, the Kashmir Valley and Ladakh.

! scope="row" | |1901–1955 1970–2010 |Flag of North-West Frontier Province |A traditional green flag, with the provincial emblem in the centre. The emblem shows a castle and a crescent moon. Underneath it are the letters NWFP – an abbreviation of the province.

! scope="row" | |2011–2018 |Flag of Federally Administered Tribal Areas |A traditional green flag, with the provincial emblem in the centre. The emblem shows a castle and two swords. Underneath it are the letters FATA – an abbreviation of the province. |}

! scope="row" | | rowspan="2" |2007–present | rowspan="2" |Flags of the Tehreek-e-Taliban-e-Pakistan |A plain white field with the full Shahada written in black across the top; below, the name of the party in Urdu is written with diacritics in black along with a black sword below it.

! scope="row" | |A inverted variant of the flag of the Islamic State, a plain white flag with the black text لا إله إلا الله (There is no God but Allah), with a black circle below it containing the white text محمد رسول الله (Muhammad is the messenger of Allah).
! scope="row" | |1992–present |Flag of Tehreek-e-Nafaz-e-Shariat-e-Mohammadi |A black field with a white circle in the centre.
! scope="row" | |2004–present |Flag of Lashkar-e-Islam |A plain black field with the name of the organisation in Urdu written in white in the centre.

! scope="row" | |1996–2025 |Flag of Lashkar-e-Jhangvi |A flag divided into two sections. The top part has three white and three black horizontal stripes. The lower section of the flag is a plain red field with فقاتلو لمتہ الکفر (Fight the leaders of disbelief), from Surah at-Tawbah, verse 12, written in white and a sword below in the centre.

! scope="row" | |?–present |Flag of the Sipah-e-Sahaba Pakistan |A flag with five horizontal black stripes and four horizontal white stripes in the top hoist and a plain red section in the lower hoist; the rest is a green field with a crescent moon and a star that has محّمدرسولﷲﷺ (Muhammad is the messenger of Allah, Peace be upon him) written in the centre. Written in the rays of the star are: ابوبکر صدیق رضی الله تعالیٰ عنه, عمر فاروق رضی الله تعالیٰ عنه, عثمان غنی رضي الله تعالیٰ عنه, علی المرتضیٰ رضي الله تعالیٰ عنه, امیر معاویہ رضی الله تعالیٰ عنه
! scope="row" | |1997–present |Flag of the Turkistan Islamic Party |A blue flag with the Shahada in white and a white crescent and star below it.

! scope="row" | |2000s–present |Flag used by rebels groups in Pakistan including: Islamic State – Khorasan Province, Jundallah (Pakistan), Islamic Movement of Uzbekistan |A plain black flag with the white text لا إله إلا الله (There is no God but Allah), with a white circle below it containing the black text محمد رسول الله (Muhammad is the messenger of Allah).
! scope="row" | |1988–present |Flag used by rebel groups including: al-Qaeda, Jamaat-ul-Ahrar, Islamic Movement of Uzbekistan |A plain black flag with the Shahada written in white on it.

! scope="row" | |2000s–present |Flag of various Balochi separatist groups including: Balochistan Liberation Army, Baluch Liberation Front, Lashkar-e-Balochistan, Baloch Nationalist Army |A horizontal bicolour of green and red, overlaid by a blue triangle at the hoist containing a white star.

candidates.section: Flag proposals > Provincial and territorial proposals
candidates.file: Proposed Flag of Islamabad Capital Territory.svg
candidates.text: ! scope="row" | |September 19, 2004 |Proposed and unofficial flag of the Islamabad Capital Territory by Dr. Tariq Saleem Marwat |A diagonal tricolour. A triangle of green in the upper fly half, containing a white star and crescent; a stripe of white followed by black in the lower hoist half. The diagonal design differentiates it from the national flag. The square shape makes the triangles symmetric. Black is added to give it a distinct look. Black was the colour used for the flag at the time of Muhammad's conquest of Mecca. |}
